To determine whether Ivan the Terrible used the Byzantine calendar, we can look at the calendar system used in Russia during his reign (1533–1584). 

1. During the medieval and early modern periods, the Russian Orthodox Church and the Russian state used the Byzantine calendar (also known as the "Creation of the World" calendar or Anno Mundi). 
2. In this calendar, time was calculated from the creation of the world, which was placed at September 1, 5509 BC, and the New Year began on September 1.
3. Ivan the Terrible, as the Grand Prince of Moscow and the first Tsar of All Russia, lived and ruled within this exact chronological system. Russia did not switch to the Julian calendar (counting from the birth of Christ) until Peter the Great decreed it in December 1699, taking effect in 1700.
4. Therefore, Ivan the Terrible did indeed use the Byzantine calendar.

Final answer: Yes
